message: Here is a 5-slide deck on rolling out HTTP/3: the rollout as a dated timeline, the canary's results in one KPI band, and what each team must do before the May step.

deck_spec.title: Rolling Out HTTP/3 Across the Public Website
deck_spec.audience: The web platform team and the teams whose services sit behind the public website
deck_spec.purpose: Agree the HTTP/3 rollout dates and each team's part, on the strength of the canary's results
deck_spec.argument: The canary shows HTTP/3 makes the public website faster and more reliable on mobile and on poor networks, so the rollout should widen to every static asset in May 2026 and to every page in July
deck_spec.call_to_action: Approve the May 2026 step, and have each team finish its part before then
narrative_arc: Open on the goal: a faster, more reliable public website on every network
Lay out the rollout as four dated milestones
Show why the results justify widening the rollout in May
Close with what each team must do before the May step

resolved_data.synthesis: On the canary (5% of traffic) time to first byte at the 75th percentile fell from 420 ms to 310 ms, connection setup on mobile was 38% faster, page-load errors on poor networks fell 22%, and 61% of canary requests were served over HTTP/3. The rollout dates are the user's plan: the canary in March 2026, every static asset in May 2026, every page in July 2026, and the TCP-only edge configuration retired in October 2026.

slides.purpose: Open the deck: rolling out HTTP/3 across the public website
slides.content_brief: Cover slide with the title 'Rolling Out HTTP/3 Across the Public Website' and a subtitle promising a faster site on mobile and on poor networks
slides.assumes: The audience runs the public website or a service behind it
slides.hands_off: HTTP/3 is worth rolling out to the whole site
slides.look: Meridian cover: the title large on the left and the subtitle beneath it; no deck-style pieces

slides.purpose: Lay out the rollout as four dated milestones
slides.content_brief: The rollout as a timeline, left to right: a canary on 5% of traffic in March 2026, every static asset in May 2026, every page in July 2026, and the TCP-only edge configuration retired in October 2026; a one-line note beneath that each step waits for the previous step's results
slides.assumes: The audience knows HTTP/3 is running as a canary
slides.hands_off: The rollout has four dated steps, and May is the next one
slides.look: Slide title above a dk-timeline of the four milestones, left to right, each opening with its date; a dk-note beneath it on each step waiting for the last

slides.content_brief: The canary's four results in one band: time to first byte at the 75th percentile down from 420 ms to 310 ms, connection setup on mobile 38% faster, page-load errors on poor networks down 22%, and 61% of canary requests served over HTTP/3; the source beneath: the canary on 5% of traffic
slides.assumes: The audience has seen the rollout plan
slides.hands_off: On the canary, HTTP/3 was faster and failed less
slides.look: Slide title above a dk-kpi-band of the four results, a dk-kpi-value and a dk-kpi-label each (four figures, one more than the template's three stat cards hold); a dk-note beneath it naming the canary as the source

slides.purpose: Show why the results justify widening the rollout in May
slides.content_brief: Three bullets, each tying a result to the decision: faster first bytes, faster connections on mobile and fewer errors on poor networks; the takeaway beneath: the canary has earned the May step
slides.assumes: The audience has seen what the canary measured
slides.hands_off: The results justify widening the rollout in May
slides.look: Three bullets on the left, one per result; the takeaway in the template's callout beneath them

slides.purpose: Close with what each team must do before the May step
slides.content_brief: What each team must do before May 2026, one bullet each: the web platform team widens HTTP/3 to every static asset, the service teams check their health checks over HTTP/3, and support learns to spot a browser falling back to HTTP/2; end with the call to action
slides.assumes: The audience has seen the plan and the results
slides.hands_off: Approve the May step, and each team finishes its part before then
slides.look: Three short bullets, one per team; the call to action in the template's callout beneath them
